shorts.title: Megalodon Ate the Predators That Ate Other Predators
shorts.outro: Every other ocean is in the full dive. It is linked below.
shorts.description: Nitrogen locked in fossil teeth gave Megalodon the highest food-chain score ever measured, so Doug drops into its sea at sunset to see what that means up close.

shorts.hook: For a century, nobody knew where this spiral of teeth went.
shorts.title: Helicoprion's Tooth Spiral Took 114 Years to Figure Out
shorts.outro: What happens next is even worse. The full dive is linked below.
shorts.description: Scientists put Helicoprion's buzz-saw whorl on its nose, tail, fin and throat until 2013 X-ray scans found it in the lower jaw, and Doug still guesses the tail.

shorts.hook: This fossil fish died with a two-meter fish inside it.
shorts.title: This Prehistoric Fish Probably Died From Its Own Dinner
shorts.outro: The next sea is much worse. The full dive is linked below.
shorts.description: A Xiphactinus fossil holds an undigested two-meter fish in its ribcage, which suggests the meal killed it soon after, so Doug lets one swallow him whole.
